claim: For every integer \(a\ge1\), among all nonnegative-integer edge-weighted \(K_6\) in which every five-vertex set has total edge weight at most \(10a+4\), the largest product strictly below the maximum is \(a^{10}(a+1)^4(a+2)\); up to vertex relabeling, it is attained uniquely by one edge of weight \(a+2\), a disjoint \(4\)-cycle whose four edges have weight \(a+1\), and the remaining ten edges of weight \(a\).

integrity.computational_claims: No computational enumeration is claimed or used.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact averaging, integer-product smoothing, and equality-structure arguments.
integrity.provenance: The cited literature motivates the parameter family; the second-product claim is established by the proof included in RESULT.md.

scientific_limitations: The exact second-product statement is restricted to six vertices, five-vertex constraints with bound \(10a+4\), and integers \(a\ge1\).
No result is claimed for larger vertex sets, other constraint values, or a general stability theorem.
title: The exact second product layer for six-vertex locally sparse multigraphs
